### Bug fixes (all in `skills/compose/references/`)

**`production-crash-playbook.md` §5 (derivedStateOf)** — GOOD example's `remember{}` had no keys:
- Before: `val filteredItems by remember { derivedStateOf { allItems.filter { it.name.contains(filter) } } }`
- After: `val filteredItems by remember(allItems, filter) { derivedStateOf { allItems.filter { it.name.contains(filter) } } }`

**`production-crash-playbook.md` §4 (dedup-index)** — `withDedupIndex()` mutated `dedupIndex` in place via `.also{}`; if the same `Notification` instance appeared twice in the source list (aliased reference), the second write would silently overwrite the first occurrence's index since both list entries pointed at the same object, reintroducing the exact duplicate-key crash the pattern exists to prevent.
- Before: `item.also { it.dedupIndex = count }`
- After: `item.copy().also { it.dedupIndex = count }` (added comment explaining why `copy()` is needed first)

**`production-crash-playbook.md` §7 (SafeShimmerItem)** — the `runCatching { Canvas(...) { ... } }` wrapper only guards the composable's registration; the `DrawScope` lambda actually runs later in the draw phase, so a draw-time failure is never caught and the `result.isFailure` fallback branch was dead code — contradicting the section's stated guarantee of a solid-color fallback.
- Before: `Box(...) { val result = runCatching { Canvas(modifier = Modifier.matchParentSize()) { if (size.minDimension <= 0f) return@Canvas; drawRect(brush = brush) } }; if (result.isFailure) { Box(...background fallback...) } }`
- After: replaced with `BoxWithConstraints` that checks `maxWidth > 0.dp && maxHeight > 0.dp` *before* attempting to draw (mirroring Section 3's fix pattern), rendering `Canvas` when the size is known and the solid-color fallback otherwise. Also reworded the trailing "Rule" line to state that draw-phase failures aren't catchable via `try/catch`/`runCatching` around the composable call.

**`performance.md`** — the "RIGHT" per-item lambda example (`Stabilize Per-Item Lambdas with remember(item.id)`) captured `onItemClick` directly inside `remember(item.id) { { onItemClick(item) } }`; since the remember key was only `item.id`, a changed `onItemClick` reference (e.g. a fresh lambda from a recomposed parent) would never invalidate the cached inner lambda, so clicks kept calling a stale callback.
- Before: `val onClick = remember(item.id) { { onItemClick(item) } }`
- After: added `val currentOnItemClick by rememberUpdatedState(onItemClick)` and changed the remembered lambda to `remember(item.id) { { currentOnItemClick(item) } }`, with a comment explaining the stale-capture reasoning.

**`animation-recipes.md`** — the shimmer example animated `x` over a fixed pixel range (`-1000f..1000f`) and built the gradient with a fixed 500px band (`Offset(x, 0f)` to `Offset(x + 500f, 0f)`), coordinates that are local to the element's own draw bounds. On any element narrower than that hard-coded band, the gradient stops sit outside the local `[0, width]` range for most of the animation cycle, so the highlight never visibly sweeps across the element — contradicting the documented "shimmer effect."
- Before: `val x by transition.animateFloat(initialValue = -1000f, targetValue = 1000f, ...)` used inside `background(Brush.linearGradient(..., start = Offset(x, 0f), end = Offset(x + 500f, 0f)))`
- After: animate a normalized `progress` (0f..1f), then use `Modifier.drawWithCache` to read the actual `size.width` and compute `bandWidth = size.width / 2f` and `x = -bandWidth + progress * (size.width + bandWidth)`, drawing via `onDrawBehind { drawRect(brush = brush) }` — so the sweep always scales to the element's real size.
